_what_this_is: Records the version of each upstream dependency that a human has actually REVIEWED. A test asserts each of these equals the version the build RESOLVED. Every dependency floats to latest at build time, so when upstream publishes, that test goes red and the release gate cannot pass until this file is updated.
_stop_before_you_edit_this_file: Read UPSTREAM-REVIEW.md and follow it. Bumping a version here without doing the review defeats the only mechanism that catches upstream behaviour changes, renamed config keys and changed defaults. None of those are visible to the golden tools/list snapshot, and loadConfig is a bare JSON.parse with no schema validation, so a renamed key is discarded in silence.
_notes_are_not_optional: Every bump records what changed, what was adopted, and what was explicitly declined and why. A decline with a reason is worth as much as an adoption: it stops the same question being re-litigated at the next bump. An empty note is a review that did not happen.
_this_file_is_gated: Not by a prompt. Editing this file is unrestricted; what is gated is the RELEASE. The build regenerates four snapshots from the resolved payload -- tools/list, --help, config.d.ts, browsers.json -- and diffs them, runs the full suite, and asserts that this file adjudicates whatever actually moved and answers every manual re-verification row by name. An entry that ignores what the build observed fails the build. See TESTING.md, 'The upstream-review gate'.
_correction_2026_08_15: An earlier version of the note above said a PreToolUse hook asks a human to approve every edit, and that a sub-agent attempting one is killed silently. Both halves were wrong, and measurement disproved them: under permission_mode 'bypassPermissions' a hook's 'ask' returned to a sub-agent is silently downgraded to ALLOW -- the edit lands unprompted, and the gate was inert against exactly the caller most likely to need it. A sub-agent did die during that work, but not from the hook; the cause is unknown and its transcript was zero bytes. Recorded because a confident wrong explanation is worse than an admitted gap, which is the same rule this file applies to versions.

Reviewed 0.0.81 -> 0.0.82 on 2026-09-21, end to end per UPSTREAM-REVIEW.md, against the payload the build re-resolved. 0.0.82 was published 2026-09-18T23:38:28.161Z. ALL FOUR GOLDEN SNAPSHOTS MOVED and every difference is adjudicated below.

THE ROLL ENDED THE DATED playwright-core OVERRIDE, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THIS REVIEW. 0.0.82 declares playwright-core AND playwright at 1.64.0-alpha-1789764292000, whose bundle carries the --file-paths fix the override was taken for on 2026-09-17. The `overrides` block and its `//overrides` note are deleted from build/payload/package.json, the wrapper's own pin floats again, and the two instruments that existed only to announce the exit are RETIRED rather than left standing: PayloadTests.TheDatedPlaywrightCoreOverrideIsStillNeeded, PayloadTests.TheExpiryComparisonFiresInBothDirections, and the Compare-PlaywrightVersion / Split-Version ordering in build/Build-Payload.ps1. THE ORDERING WAS NOT WIDENED AND WILL NOT BE. It parsed <major>.<minor>.<patch>[-alpha-YYYY-MM-DD] and THREW on anything else; the version the wrapper actually rolled to is a 13-digit epoch-milliseconds alpha it refused by design, and that refusal was correct -- silently calling an unorderable shape 'lower' is what would have kept an override alive past its own exit. Nothing in this tree ranks a playwright-core version now; every comparison left is for IDENTITY against another recorded string, so a version is an opaque string and its shape is upstream's business. The invariant that survives is the one that was always the real one and it came back to where it started: PayloadTests.TheLockRecordsUpstreamsOwnExactPinOfPlaywrightCore now asserts resolved == declared again, planted red 2026-09-21 against a doctored lock, and build/Build-Payload.ps1 makes the same check against the live resolution.

THE CHANGE THAT NO SNAPSHOT COULD HAVE SHOWN, AND IT IS THE LARGEST THING IN THIS ROLL. `tools/list` IS NO LONGER A STATIC SURFACE. createServer now declares capabilities.tools.listChanged TRUE and its ListTools handler ends with a push of backend.dynamicTools(); dynamicTools returns the CURRENT TAB's WebMCP tools, named `webmcp_` + the page's own tool name sanitised and cut at 64 characters. So a WEB PAGE can add tools to the child's advertised list, with its own descriptions and its own inputSchemas, and the server sends notifications/tools/list_changed when the page's set changes. In the same release, every snapshot-bearing tool result began carrying the page's tool listing INSIDE the snapshot -- a `- webmcp tools (page-provided, untrusted):` block, then per tool the page's name, its [readOnly]/[consequential] annotations, its full description and its inputSchema as JSON -- and the tab header carries `- N webmcp tools available on the page`. The collection runs wherever _includeSnapshot is not 'none', which is most tools rather than only browser_snapshot, by evaluating collectToolsInPage in EVERY FRAME of the current tab, each bounded at 5,000 ms.

THAT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN READ, THREE WAYS, and the rig and the transcripts are kept: docs/probes/2026-09-21-webmcp and docs/evidence/2026-09-21-webmcp, with the finding in kb/playwright/tools-and-artifacts.md and re-verification row 133. Against a page registering two WebMCP tools, the CHILD's tools/list went 72 -> 74 and sent three list_changed notifications; with `webmcp: false` written, 72 -> 72, no notification, no header line and no snapshot block. THROUGH THE PUBLISHED BrowserAI.Server.exe, BOTH HALVES OF THE EXPOSURE ARE CLOSED AND ONE IS NOT. BrowserAI's tools/list was 78 BEFORE the page and 78 AFTER -- nothing was added -- because BrowserAI answers tools/list from THE RUN'S OWN CHILD, which never navigates and so has no page to collect from. And a tools/call naming webmcp_probe_tool_alpha was refused at the door with the unjudged-tool refusal, nothing forwarded and nothing started, which is deny-by-default meeting a name A WEB PAGE INVENTED. Neither mechanism was built for this and both hold. BrowserAI's own initialize still advertises an empty tools capability object, so the child's listChanged is not forwarded and no list_changed reaches a caller, which is correct because BrowserAI's list genuinely does not change.

WHAT IS NOT CLOSED IS THE TEXT, AND IT IS REPORTED RATHER THAN DECIDED. Tool results are forwarded verbatim by design, so the page's own tool names, descriptions and schemas now arrive in every snapshot-bearing result. Upstream's [UNTRUSTED: ...] prefix is on the dynamic tool DESCRIPTIONS rather than on the snapshot block, which is labelled only `(page-provided, untrusted)`. `webmcp: false` removes all of it and BrowserAI writes no `webmcp` key today, so upstream's default is in force. THIS IS A PRODUCT STANCE UNDER THE WRITTEN-RATHER-THAN-OMITTED DOCTRINE, the same class as `timeouts.idle` and `imageResponses` on 2026-09-15, and it belongs to the maintainer. It is raised with alternatives rather than taken here.

NEW CLI FLAG: --no-webmcp, "do not collect or expose the tools that a page registers through the WebMCP API." Never built; BrowserAI configures through a generated config file and builds no flags.

It carries the COUNT ONLY and none of the page's text, but it reaches the model through every tab header regardless of what tool-verdicts.json says about the two tools, so denying them yields a model told that N tools are available and a product that refuses both. REPORTED AND NOT CLOSED BY THE DENY, again, because it is upstream's: renderTabHeader's `- N webmcp tools available on the page` still reaches the model. It carries the count and none of the page's text. (2) timeouts.idle (Q177 = a): ADOPTED, WRITTEN EXPLICITLY AT UPSTREAM'S OWN DEFAULT of 3,600,000 ms, under the written-rather-than-omitted doctrine that already governs allowUnrestrictedFileAccess. DECLINED, each with its reason: (1) the two task-runner commits (#65217 escaping Windows environment variables, #64907 matching cmd.exe case-insensitively) -- that is node --run, which nothing here invokes; (2) the 16 stream commits -- overwhelmingly web streams and their hot paths, which playwright-core does not use for a piped child, and the classic-stream items are covered by the real-child and smoke tiers rather than by reading them; (3) every SEMVER-MINOR in the release -- crypto STORE-loader private keys, the histogram rework, net.BlockList performance, perf_hooks hypothesis testing, util.MIMEType.parse -- none is on a path BrowserAI takes, and NODE_OPTIONS and NODE_PATH are refused at ChildEnvironment.Refused so no new flag can arrive through the environment; (4) 'deps: update Undici to 7.29.1' -- playwright-core brings its own HTTP for the CDN, and nothing here calls fetch from node; (5) 'tty: add raw-vt and io raw modes' -- the child's stdio are pipes and every launch in this tree sets CreateNoWindow, so there is no tty to put in a raw mode; (6) npm is unchanged in any case, and the payload extracts only node.exe and LICENSE from the archive, so the bundled npm ships nowhere and resolves nothing. RE-VERIFICATION (kb/re-verification.md), every row a Node move puts in play, answered by name: rows 2 and 2b (job containment end to end, and from the published NativeAOT binary) -- ANSWERED GREEN by the gate under v24.21.0, ILCompiler 10.0.12 and SDK 10.0.401; row 21 (payload sizes) -- the two PAYLOAD rows were re-measured by this build and both figures are updated in place, and the FOUR BROWSER figures are OWED AND NOT RUN because both browser revisions moved, which the row now says in place rather than carrying the old numbers forward as if they still held; row 26 (payload licensing as shipped) -- re-read, Node's LICENSE is still the single aggregated file at the same size and the payload's licensing composition is unchanged; row 46 (Node's LICENSE is not published beside node.exe, and the extraction is keyed on the archive path) -- ANSWERED by the build, which found and extracted node-v24.21.0-win-x64/LICENSE and would have thrown had the archive been restructured; row 49 (npm lock keying, and npm ci not rewriting the lock) -- ANSWERED, the rebuild parsed the lock with -AsHashtable and npm ci left it byte-identical, which the build asserts rather than observes; row 50 (PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD gates only the postinstall paths) -- ANSWERED, and for the first time on a build that actually installed: the variable was set throughout and the explicit install-browser chromium still provisioned, which is the behaviour the payload build's comment predicts and the reason it fails loudly on the chrome.exe assertion if upstream ever extends the gate; row 85 (the update lane's own numbers) -- OWED AND STILL NOT RUN, and the kb entry says so in place, dated, now naming a THREE-sided gap rather than one: node.exe +198,656 on the day and +754,688 since the figures were taken, the payload mcp tree DOWN 373,255, and the published BrowserAI.exe at 19,186,688 against the recorded 17,853,952. NOT ONE FIGURE WAS ADJUSTED, and the two payload halves moved in opposite directions, so there is not even a single delta a reader could be tempted to add. Rows 16 and 16a are NOT in play: their trigger is an SDK change to the discover probe, not a Node move. Row 102 IS in play but on the @playwright/mcp axis rather than this one, and it is answered in the playwright-core entry -- it ARRIVED. v26 is Current rather than LTS and is deliberately not tracked; it read v26.8.2 on this date.
